public_rationale: Microsoft reported $39.4 billion in cash paid for property, plant and equipment for July–September 2026 [e2]. This company-wide measure does not establish whether all four companies deliberately retreated from the specified infrastructure spending [e2]. It also does not establish supplier-market effects attributable to such a retreat, leaving the conditional forecast unresolved [e2].
limitations: The evidence covers Microsoft's spending and does not establish qualifying spending decisions by all four companies or subsequent supplier-market effects [e2].
Cash paid for property, plant and equipment does not isolate the specified categories; Microsoft separately reports finance-lease commencements [e2].
The contract retains ambiguity about whether the $30 billion threshold applies individually or collectively, and about accounting basis, contraction magnitude, duration and response lag.
The forecast has no deadline; under the contract, passage of time alone cannot contradict it.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is a deliberate retreat by the four named companies from quarterly infrastructure spending of at least $30 billion each.
The collective-spending reading is also possible and must be retained as an ambiguity.
The consequence means a substantial, sustained contraction in semiconductor and related supplier demand and sales caused by the spending retreat.
A delivery delay, accounting reclassification, or isolated stock-market decline does not by itself establish either the condition or the consequence.
criteria.support_condition: The specified spending retreat occurs, followed by a substantial contraction in relevant supplier demand and sales attributable to it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The spending retreat occurs and its completed effects are absorbed without substantial contraction in relevant supplier demand and sales.
